Q5614259.label: 1927 Guatemalan Constitutional Convention election
Q5614259.summary: Constitutional Convention elections were held in Guatemala in June 1927. Lázaro Chacón González put 33 senior officers on the official list of candidates, and whilst civilian leaders of the Liberal Party were also on it, the fact that most of them were members of the armed forces suggested that González was determined to dominate the convention.

Q681139.label: 1993 Polish parliamentary election
Q681139.desc: parliamentary elections in Poland made after dissolution of the parliament
Q681139.summary: Parliamentary elections were held in Poland on 19 September 1993. All 460 members of the Sejm and 100 senators of the Senate were elected. The elections were won by the left-wing parties of the Democratic Left Alliance and the Polish People's Party, who formed a coalition government. The coalition was just four seats short of a supermajority.

Q928435.label: National Movement for Stability and Progress
Q928435.wiki: National Movement for Stability and Progress
Q928435.summary: The National Movement for Stability and Progress is a liberal, populist political party in Bulgaria. It was known as the National Movement Simeon II until 3 June 2007.

Q4996275.label: 1938 Bulgarian parliamentary election
Q4996275.summary: Parliamentary elections were held in Bulgaria to elect members of the XXIV Ordinary National Assembly between 6 and 27 March 1938, the first after the 1934 coup. The elections were held on a non-partisan basis, with all parties banned. Pro-government candidates won a majority of seats. Voter turnout was 70%. Women were allowed to vote – for the first time – if they were married, divorced or widowed.

Q4832435.label: 2000–2001 Azerbaijani parliamentary election
Q4832435.summary: Parliamentary elections were held in Azerbaijan on 5 November 2000, although a re-run had to be held in 11 constituencies on 7 January 2001 due to "massive irregularities". In the lead-up to the election, the authoritarian Heydar Aliyev regime banned seven opposition parties from contesting the election.

Q349875.label: 1983 Turkish embassy attack in Lisbon
Q349875.summary: The 1983 Turkish embassy attack was an attack on the Turkish embassy in Lisbon on 27 July 1983, which resulted in the death of 7 people, including all 5 attackers.

mentions.c: Portugal: Terrorist attack: 1983 Turkish embassy attack in Lisbon

Q1367731.label: Saudi–Yemeni War
Q1367731.desc: war between Saudi Arabia and the Kingdom of Yemen in 1934
Q1367731.summary: The Saudi–Yemeni war was a war between the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia and the Kingdom of Yemen in 1934.

Q18651827.label: Battle of Baotou
Q18651827.desc: 1939 battle of the Second Sino-Japanese War
Q18651827.summary: The Battle of Baotou was fought from 17 to 24 December 1939 in Suiyuan Province, Republic of China as part of the Second Sino-Japanese War. Taking place in the Eighth War Area in Northern China, the engagement was part of the wider 1939–1940 Winter Offensive by the National Revolutionary Army.

Q18657971.label: Battle of West Suiyuan
Q18657971.summary: The Battle of West Suiyuan was part of the Second Sino-Japanese War. It was fought from January – February 1940 during the Chinese 1939 Winter Offensive.

Q2890419.label: Battle of Yenangyaung
Q2890419.summary: The Battle of Yenangyaung was fought in Burma from 16 to 19 April 1942. As part of the Burma Campaign of World War II, the battle was fought between Chinese and British allied forces on one side and Japanese forces on the other. The battle took place in the vicinity of Yenangyaung and its oil fields.

Q16849587.label: Japanese invasion of Aparri
Q16849587.desc: overview of the Japanese invasion of Aparri
Q16849587.summary: The Japanese Invasion of Aparri on 10 December, 1941, was one in a series of advance landings made by Imperial Japanese forces as a first step in their invasion of the Philippines. The purpose was to obtain control of local air strips, which could be used as forward bases by fighter aircraft for operations further south. The first invasion was at Batan Island on 8 December 1941. This was followed by Vigan, Legaspi, Davao, and Jolo Island over the next few days

Q6135475.label: Operation Karbala 10
Q6135475.summary: Operation Karbala 10 was a joint operation by Iran and Kurdish PUK rebels in Iraq.

Q4872371.label: Battle of Shok Valley
Q4872371.img: Operational Detachment Alpha 3336, 3rd Special Forces Group (Airborne) recon Shok Valley, Afghanistan, Dec. 15, 2008.jpg
Q4872371.summary: The Battle of Shok Valley, also known as Operation Commando Wrath, was a joint U.S.-Afghan raid designed to kill or capture Gulbuddin Hekmatyar, the leader of Hezb-e-Islami Gulbuddin (HIG) in the Shok Valley of Nuristan Province of Afghanistan on 6 April 2008. Ten soldiers belonging to U.S Army special forces and their combat cameraman were awarded the Silver Star for bravery, the greatest number of such awards for a single battle since the Vietnam War. In 2018, Special Forces medic Ronald J. Shurer's Silver Star was upgraded to the Medal of Honor for his actions during the battle.

Q3354803.label: Operation Panther's Claw
Q3354803.desc: British military operation of the Afghan War in Helmand Province
Q3354803.summary: Operation Panchai Palang, or Panther's Claw, was a coalition military operation of the War in Afghanistan in Helmand Province in southern Afghanistan. It aimed to secure various canal and river crossings to establish a permanent International Security Assistance Force (ISAF) presence in the area. The commander of the operation declared the first stage a success on 27 July 2009.

Q25267.label: degree Celsius
Q25267.summary: The degree Celsius is the unit of temperature on the Celsius temperature scale, one of two temperature scales used in the International System of Units (SI), the other being the closely related Kelvin scale. The degree Celsius can refer to a specific point on the Celsius temperature scale or to a difference or range between two temperatures. It is named after the Swedish astronomer Anders Celsius (1701–1744), who proposed the first version of it in 1742. The unit was called centigrade in several languages for many years.

Q20807347.label: Princeton Neuroscience Institute
Q20807347.summary: The Princeton Neuroscience Institute (PNI) is a center for neuroscience research at Princeton University. Founded in the spring of 2004, the PNI serves as a "stimulus for teaching and research in neuroscience and related fields" and "places particular emphasis on the close connection between theory, modeling, and experimentation using the most advanced technologies." It often partners with Princeton University's departments of Psychology and Molecular Biology.

Q691.label: Papua New Guinea
aliases: Independent State of Papua New Guinea
Q691.summary: Papua New Guinea (PNG), officially the Independent State of Papua New Guinea, is an island nation in Oceania that comprises the eastern half of the island of New Guinea and offshore islands in Melanesia, a region of the southwestern Pacific Ocean north of Australia. It has a land border with Indonesia to the west and maritime borders with Australia to the south and the Solomon Islands to the east. Its capital is Port Moresby. The country's 462,840 km2 (178,700 mi2) includes a large mainland and hundreds of islands.

Q871091.label: British Malaya
Q871091.desc: set of states on Peninsular Malaysia and island of Singapore under British dominance from 18th to 20th centuries
Q871091.summary: The term British Malaya loosely describes a set of states on the lower Malay Peninsula and the island of Singapore that were brought under British hegemony or control between the late 18th and the mid-20th century.
